source.title: Investigating the Indirect Object Identification circuit in Mamba

record.tranche_reason: The study applies circuit-finding and intervention techniques to IOI in Mamba, a different model architecture, and reports findings about its mechanism and prompt settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports IOI results for Mamba and, briefly, layer-removal robustness for GPT-2-Small. Its findings concern a Mamba convolution/SSM mechanism, not the GPT-2 small 26-head circuit. It does not test backup heads or compare GPT-2 circuit-finding methods directly. Statements about methods or metrics being useful choices, without an outcome on the circuit or IOI behavior, are not separate rows.
record.test_reason: The study asks whether IOI in a different architecture (state-spaces/mamba-370m) runs through an identifiable circuit, so it bears loosely on V3. It is not a direct test, because it never maps GPT-2 head classes or roles onto Mamba components. The other versions concern the GPT-2 small circuit, its evaluation, or its prompt variants, and are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors partially reverse-engineer Mamba's IOI circuit: layer 39 is a bottleneck, its conv shifts names forward, names are stored linearly in its SSM, and outputs go to the last token. They take this as initial evidence that circuit tools transfer to Mamba, with more analysis needed.
record.recipe_differences: The study adapts resample ablation, layer removal, cross-talk analysis, EAP, and ACDC to state-spaces/mamba-370m. It studies a convolution/SSM architecture rather than GPT-2 small's attention-head circuit and does not reproduce the original head-class analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper uses Normalized Logit Diff for patching and accuracy for layer removal and circuit evaluations. It states that results are shown separately by corruption and template, and that results for two-name templates can be misleading. It also notes that cross-talk removal is only a proxy and does not eliminate cross-talk shared by clean and corrupted prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing the layer that hurts accuracy least, repeatedly, lets about half of Mamba's layers be dropped with minimal accuracy loss. The authors say they replicated this on GPT-2 small, without reporting numbers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI accuracy is robust to removing about half of a model's layers (layer-level redundancy).

fits_no_version.finding: Mamba's layer-39 SSM represents names linearly; subtract-and-add editing flips the output more than 95% of the time.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Entity names in Mamba's IOI bottleneck layer are linearly represented and steerable.

record.problems: The study focuses on one Mamba model. Several intervention results are presented only in figures without exact values in the text. Resample-ablation experiments are limited to templates sharing name token positions; the authors note that cross-talk removal is only a proxy, that their cosine-similarity evidence is not causal, and that more circuit analysis is needed. The study does not test the GPT-2 small head circuit directly.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results were left out. The reported GPT-2-Small layer-removal robustness is not a result on whether the versions' specified head classes or roles carry IOI, so it is not included as a row.

untested.parts: Whether Mamba has analogues of duplicate-token, S-inhibition or name-mover roles; other sizes and checkpoints; reuse of components for other tasks.
The entire version; the GPT-2 small head circuit is not examined.
The entire version. The authors only speculate about 'backup behaviour' in Mamba (R10).
The entire version; there is no comparison of methods on the GPT-2 circuit.
The entire version for the GPT-2 circuit. The remark that 2-name templates are misleading gives no outcome on the circuit.
The entire version for the GPT-2 circuit.

missing.what: GPT-2 small layer-removal robustness replication (no numbers given)

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked many Mamba rows to V5 and V6. Those versions concern the GPT-2 circuit's evaluation and prompt variants; within-Mamba results don't test them, so the links were removed. The V3 label 'challenges' was downgraded to 'limits_scope' for two reasons. First, the study never searches for role analogues. Second, an attention-free architecture cannot host head classes, so the result marks a boundary of V3 rather than a failed replication. Most numbers are figure-only, there is one model, and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The GPT-2 small 26-head, 7-class circuit and its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria are not tested.
The study does not ablate GPT-2 name-mover heads or test backup-head self-repair.
The paper studies one Mamba model, not multiple sizes or checkpoints, and does not test reuse of components for other tasks.
The study does not compare alternative methods, ablation types, or metrics on the GPT-2 small circuit to determine whether they recover essentially the same circuit.
The study reports evaluation choices and qualifications for Mamba, not a controlled sensitivity analysis of the original GPT-2 circuit or its criteria.
Prompt experiments use three-name templates; the paper does not establish the same mechanism for more than three names or all name orders and templates.

rows.subject: state-spaces/mamba-370m
rows.operation_detail: Patch all layers' token cross-talk, then iteratively unpatch the layer that improves accuracy most to form a minimal cross-talk circuit.

rows.note: The authors say layer 39 is always the first layer added and has a large effect. They caution that the procedure removes only task-relevant cross-talk specific to the uncorrupted prompt.
rows.check: Layers 39 and 15 appear in every minimal cross-talk circuit. This is a layer-level bottleneck, not the GPT-2 multi-class head structure. 'Across templates' is within Mamba, not a test of V6 on the GPT-2 circuit, so the V5/V6 links are removed.

relationships.reason: Per the text, Mamba's IOI runs through a layer-39 conv/SSM bottleneck (plus layers 0 and 15) writing to the last token. Head-class roles cannot apply, and the study maps none (R1, R3, R4, R8, R9).
relationships.display_finding: IOI computation passes through a layer-39 convolutional and state-space bottleneck, with layers 0 and 15 also contributing to the final-token representation; correspondence to GPT-2 head roles remains untested.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.reason: R1, R3, R4, R8 and R9 identify Mamba mechanisms without testing whether the named GPT-2 head-class roles recur. Their cannot_determine states are appropriate; an untested role mapping cannot justify limits_scope.

relation.reason: The paper cites Wang et al. for the IOI task and ablation precedents, but neither evaluates nor uses the established GPT-2 attention-head circuit. Reusing the task and interpretability methods does not test the catalog's circuit claim.

tranche.reason: The study identifies mechanisms for IOI in Mamba but does not test preservation of the head classes and roles named by V3. Its other results do not test the remaining claim versions. A new architecture alone does not establish a result on the stated claim.

source_check.notes: Remove the V3 links from R1, R3, R4, R8 and R9; these findings fit none of the stated versions. The authors' conclusion is accurately summarized: partial reverse-engineering and initial evidence that circuit-analysis tools transfer to Mamba.

statements.correction: Mamba-370m: layer-39 convolution/SSM bottleneck; layers 0 and 15 also implicated; no mapping or test of GPT-2 duplicate-token, S-inhibition or name-mover roles; V3 preservation untested.
statements.problem: The factual summary is accurate, but its limits_scope classification treats an untested head-class preservation claim as negative evidence.

statements.correction: Section 4.3 and Figure 9: Subtract and Add succeeds more than 95% of the time under the criterion that the substituted name's logit exceeds the original name's logit; no corresponding argmax output-flip rate is stated.
statements.problem: More than 95% is supported for the pairwise logit substitution measure; describing it as an IOI output-flip rate overstates the reported measure.
